title: Sharks and Minnows Dribble Game
description: Minnows dribble across the court while sharks try to knock the ball away, a lively game that builds protected dribbling, vision and quick changes of direction.

content.objective: Dribble across the court under pressure, keeping the ball protected with the body and the head up.
content.setup: All minnows stand on one baseline, each with a ball. Two or three sharks stand in the middle of the court without a ball.
instructions: On the whistle the minnows dribble to the opposite baseline while the sharks try to knock the balls away.
A minnow who loses control of the ball, or has it knocked out of bounds, becomes a shark for the next round.
Minnows who reach the far baseline wait until all have crossed, then run back on the whistle.
Play until one minnow remains, then restart with new sharks.
For the final round, minnows may use only the weak hand.
coachingPoints: Keep the head up and look for open space between the sharks.
Use the body as a shield: dribble on the side away from the shark.
Change speed and direction; do not run in a straight line.
Sharks: stay low, keep your hands active, and never reach in from behind.
commonMistakes: Watching the ball instead of the sharks.
Dribbling in a straight line at full speed.
content.safety: Sharks must stay below shoulder height and play the ball only; stop the game if players collide.
progressions: Add a third shark or shrink the width of the court.
regressions: Sharks walk, or minnows may use both hands freely.
variations: Minnows must switch hands after every shark they pass.

annotations.text: Minnows cross, sharks try to steal
